**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no most-favoured-nation or most-favoured-customer obligation on Meridian Fieldworks. Targeted searches across the document ("most favoured/favourable/favorable", "MFN", "no less favo", "best pricing", "benchmark", third-party offer matching, other-customer comparisons) surfaced nothing running against us. On the contrary, § 12.3 expressly records that "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment," and preserves our freedom to engage any supplier or conduct business in any field or territory — squarely the playbook's preferred position.

Noted for context only (not a deviation): Copperleaf does not grant us an MFN either, so there is no vendor-side best-pricing commitment to preserve. That is a commercial upside we could pursue in negotiation, but its absence is not a playbook issue under this rule.
